status.en: 20 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 20 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopian forces have installed a caretaker administration in Tigray and are advancing toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced that elections will be held within six months and that Western Tigray will be settled through constitutional processes. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske styrker har installert en midlertidig administrasjon i Tigray og rykker frem mot den eritreiske grensen, mens en pro-regjeringsmilits sier at den har tatt kontroll over den regionale flyplassen og rapporterer at eritreiske styrker led tap der. USA, gjennom utenriksminister Marco Rubio, oppfordrer Etiopia og Eritrea til å dempe kampene. Ordfører i Mekelle, Shishay Amare, kunngjorde at valg vil bli holdt innen seks måneder og at Vest-Tigray vil bli løst gjennom konstitusjonelle prosesser. Konflikten forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
